name: Metropolitan Transportation Network (MTN)
whatItIs: School bus and van company founded and led by Tashitaa Tufaa, who grew up in Ethiopia's Oromo region and came to Minnesota as a refugee in 1992.
evidence: Own site published Oct. 22, 2026, lists service districts. Republican Eagle, March 27, 2026, reports a new three-year Red Wing contract with the Fridley company.

name: Mi'aawaa Bakery and Coffee Cart
neighborhoodOrCity: Mobile; owner based in Brooklyn Center
whatItIs: Chaltu Hassan's cart serving lattes, cookies and Eid boxes. The name means sweet in Oromo.
evidence: Sahan Journal, Sept. 17, 2025, describes it operating, with a photo from Aug. 13, 2025. Mpls.St.Paul Magazine's best new list for 2025 says it appeared at many markets that year. No 2026 page was found.

name: Arya Cafe
whatItIs: Coffee shop opened August 2025, described by the magazine as serving Oromian-inflected flavors. The owner is not named, so Oromo ownership is not stated.
evidence: Mpls.St.Paul Magazine's 2025 best new restaurants list. No 2026 page was found.

name: Mediterranean Deli
whatItIs: Meet Minneapolis calls it Oromo-owned and a longtime Cedar Avenue staple with Ethiopian and Middle Eastern entrees and sandwiches.
evidence: Meet Minneapolis pages are undated, and the West Bank Business Association retail list does not include it. No hours or dated post could be found. Rechecked Oct. 31, 2026: no current Minnesota page found; mediterraneandeli.com belongs to an unrelated North Carolina restaurant.

name: Sainaa Cafe
whatItIs: Family-run Ethiopian coffee shop named for an Oromo word meaning come inside and memories. Oromo ownership is not stated.
evidence: Own site, checked Oct. 31, 2026, lists a priced menu, online ordering, the 317 W. Lake St. address and Tuesday-Saturday hours (site footer reads copyright 2024). Meet Minneapolis (Sept. 27, 2022) gives the Oromo meaning of the name.

name: Community Link Services MN
whatItIs: Service provider offering information and help to Oromo and other diaspora residents, announced in Oromo Diaspora Media.
evidence: Oromo Diaspora Media post dated Oct. 8, 2026. Its own website could not be opened, and its exact services were not confirmed.

name: Oromia Health Care LLC
whatItIs: Listed home care provider for skilled nursing and in-home therapy. The listing does not state ownership or languages.
evidence: A directory listing says its data are current as of August 2026 and advises confirming license status. The provider's own page was not found. Rechecked Oct. 31, 2026: no newer page found.

name: Oromo Diaspora Media (ODM)
whatItIs: News and radio stream mainly in Afaan Oromoo, with Minnesota public agencies among listed partners.

name: Voice of Oromiyaa, KFAI
whatItIs: Weekly radio program, Sundays 5 to 6 p.m., hosted by Jelil Abdella and Said Ali.

name: Oromia Media Network
whatItIs: Nonprofit news outlet on Oromia, with $213,558 in 2024 revenue and one employee that year.
evidence: Cause IQ shows a 2024 filing and a leader listed as of Nov. 17, 2025. No dated 2026 program page was opened. Rechecked Oct. 31, 2026: oromiamedia.org now shows unrelated Thai-language content, and no current network page was found.

name: Oromia 11
whatItIs: TV network startup launched in 2021 with Tashitaa Tufaa as board chair.
evidence: Only a Feb. 3, 2021 article was opened. Rechecked Oct. 31, 2026: no newer page found.

name: Oromo Community of Minnesota building rental
whatItIs: Community center rented for gatherings, baby showers and engagement parties.
evidence: Own site lists hours and facility requests, with statements dated through Jan. 29, 2026 and an event listed for Nov. 28, 2026.

name: Bultum Academy
whatItIs: Charter school that teaches Afaan Oromo alongside regular subjects.
evidence: School jobs posted Oct. 19 and 27, 2026, on mnschooljobs.org; own site lists school hours.

name: Red Wolf Chai
type: chai maker and seller (online, farmers markets, coffee shops)
whatItIs: Chai and chapatis made from the founders' Oromo mother's recipes; named for the Ethiopian wolf of Oromia's Bale Highlands. Founded 2021 by brothers Azhar Abdusebur and Mayzer Muhammad with Mowafag Mohamed.
evidence: Own site, checked Oct. 31, 2026, takes online orders and offers catering. Sahan Journal, July 8, 2021, describes the founding and the Oromo family recipes; Meet Minneapolis's East African food guide features it to highlight Oromo culture.

name: Oromo Mall
whatItIs: Described by Oromo Diaspora Media as a large Oromo market opening for the first time in Minnesota; the post links the Tawhid Islamic Center of Minnesota beside the address.
evidence: Oromo Diaspora Media post dated March 30, 2025, announces it has started operating. No own site and no 2026 notice found, so current operation rests on that 2025 post.

name: Adama Restaurant and Awash Bakery
whatItIs: Ethiopian restaurant that Heavy Table reported in 2017 had a focus on Oromo food.
evidence: Heavy Table, November 2017. A Franki directory listing updated Aug. 14, 2026 shows daily hours but is unclaimed and aggregated; the restaurant's own site did not load.

name: Northside Grocery and Deli
whatItIs: Neighborhood store advertised on Oromo Diaspora Media as an African business. Ownership is not stated, so Oromo ownership is not claimed.
evidence: Oromo Diaspora Media notice dated June 19, 2025, with address and phone. No 2026 page found.
